name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset for land use and land cover classification based on Sentinel-2 satellite images, covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV], 2019.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in two steps: (1) satellite image acquisition and (2) dataset creation. The authors downloaded Sentinel-2A satellite images via Amazon S3, choosing images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas and distributed over 34 European countries. They selected images with low cloud level and extracted images recorded all over the year to increase variance. Based on the obtained satellite images, they created 27,000 georeferenced and labeled 64x64 image patches, which were manually checked.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of openly and freely accessible Sentinel-2A multi-spectral satellite images downloaded via Amazon S3 and associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Satellite images were recorded all over the year; specific start and end dates for dataset collection are not provided.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset creation process involved merging classes to 10 considered classes, dissolving adjacent polygons of the same class, merging multiple Sentinel-2 images, cropping 64x64 image patches, and filtering mislabeled or broken image patches.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Bands with lower spatial resolution were resampled to 10 meter resolution. For band evaluation, bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction. The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. They did not filter samples with color cast due to atmospheric effects.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of labeled image patches created based on Sentinel-2 images and the European Urban Atlas. The authors chose 10 land use and land cover classes based on visibility at 10 meters per pixel and frequency in the European Urban Atlas. They manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by removing mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice. They note that some classes are positively correlated, especially the two agricultural classes and the residential and industrial building classes, and that the classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as highway and river.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Georeferenced image locations distributed over 34 European countries.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the resulting classification system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications, including agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, environmental monitoring, land use and land cover change detection, nature protection, sustainable development, and improving geographical maps such as OpenStreetMap.
rai:dataBiases: The distribution of georeferenced images is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. The authors selected images with low cloud level and aimed to cover as many countries as possible and images recorded all over the year to capture high intra-class variance. They also note low positive correlation between some classes, especially the agricultural classes and residential versus industrial buildings.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset uses 10 meter per pixel resolution, so some classes visible in very-high-resolution imagery are difficult to distinguish. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as highway and river. A classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark and training basis for supervised machine learning and deep neural networks for land use and land cover classification using Sentinel-2 satellite images. The paper uses class-wise training/test splits, including an 80/20 split for benchmarking. The dataset can also support real-world Earth observation applications such as land use and land cover change detection and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
